name: QInvest
founded: 2007 (incorporated April 2007 and licensed by the Qatar Financial Centre Authority, per QIC's Oct 2022 release and the LinkedIn company page)
ownership_summary: Unlisted QFC company. Qatar Islamic Bank (QIB) holds 49% and accounts for it as an associate: QIB's board approved a plan on 31 Dec 2024 to dispose of part of its stake, the sale completed in 2025, QIB lost control and its holding fell from 65.62% (31 Dec 2024) to 49% (31 Dec 2025). The buyer(s) of the 16.62% and the identity of the other 51% shareholders were not found. Older company descriptions (QIC release, Oct 2022) say shareholders include QIB, other institutional investors and high-net-worth individuals. parent_id is left null because QIB does not control QInvest and equity-accounts it.
government_link: No direct government shareholder disclosed (checked 2026-10-12). Indirect only: the 49% holder, QIB, is partly owned by Qatar Investment Authority (see qa-qib.json). The QIB Group page and the 2021 appointment release name the chairman as Sheikh Jassim bin Hamad bin Jassim bin Jaber Al Thani, who is also QIB's chairman per the QIB Annual Report 2025 (S4).
group_structure: Not consolidated by QIB since 2025 (equity-accounted associate), so QInvest assets, revenue and AUM must not be added to qa-qib. qa-qib records QInvest only as an associate; QInvest's metrics, people and capabilities are in this file. Three divisions per its own descriptions: Investment Banking, Asset Management, Principal Investments (real estate, credit, equity). Joint venture: Epicure Islamic Investment Management LLC (QFCRA-regulated Islamic asset manager), 51% QIC via Epicure Holdings LLC and 49% QInvest, established Oct 2022. QIB CEO Bassel Gamal and QIB Chairman sit on the QInvest board (QIB Annual Report 2025).

subsidiaries.name: Epicure Islamic Investment Management LLC (joint venture)
subsidiaries.activity: Shari'a-compliant asset management (QFCRA-authorised); 51% owned by QIC through Epicure Holdings LLC

footprint: Headquartered in Doha (West Bay, Tornado Tower, per the LinkedIn company page). The LinkedIn page also mentions an office in Istanbul and affiliates in India and the UK (undated). QIC's Oct 2022 release says activities span the Middle East, Europe, Turkey, the UK and the USA.
customer_segments: Institutional and corporate clients (investment banking, sukuk and debt capital markets arranging, M&A advisory) and investors in its funds and principal investments. No retail or mass-affluent offer found; no published HNW or wealth-client segment (checked 2026-10-12).
business_lines: Investment Banking (advisory, M&A, equity and debt capital markets, sukuk); Asset Management; Principal Investments (real estate, credit and equity). It acted as joint lead manager and bookrunner on QIB's USD sukuk (mandate 3 Jun 2025) and, per Forbes Middle East, on QIB's USD 750m sukuk and Dukhan Bank's USD 800m five-year sukuk in 2024.

capabilities.wealth_summary: QInvest LLC is a Doha-based, QFCRA-authorised Islamic investment bank in which Qatar Islamic Bank holds 49% after a partial sale in 2025. Its stated divisions are Investment Banking, Asset Management and Principal Investments (real estate, credit and equity). Forbes Middle East put AUM of QInvest and affiliates at USD 2bn in 2024, but QInvest has published no AUM for 2025 or 2026 and its own website currently shows only a 'new website coming soon' page. It is an institutional dealmaker rather than a wealth distributor: it arranges sukuk (joint lead manager on QIB's 2025 USD sukuk mandate and, per Forbes, on QIB and Dukhan Bank deals in 2024), and it holds 49% of Epicure Islamic Investment Management with Qatar Insurance Company. No retail channel, app, brokerage, advisory-to-individuals or HNW proposition was found. The CEO post is held on an acting basis (Hussein Fakhreddine) since Co-CEO Hussain Abdulla's resignation in May 2024.

private_banking.detail: No private banking or wealth-client proposition described in QIC's Oct 2022 release, the Gulf Times Apr 2022 report or the LinkedIn company page (three divisions listed, none for private clients). A search snippet of a third-party profile mentions 'private client services' but the page was not opened.

asset_management.detail: Asset Management division. AUM USD 2bn for 'QInvest and affiliate companies' in 2024 (Forbes ME, secondary). 49% of Epicure Islamic Investment Management LLC (Shari'a-compliant, QFCRA-regulated; QIC's Epicure Investment Management supplies the asset-management expertise, QInvest the infrastructure, market reach and Islamic product experience; QIC cited USD 7bn+ managed at Epicure in 2022). A QIB director biography refers to 'several asset management funds at QInvest'; fund names and sizes were not found.

brokerage.detail: No brokerage or execution service found on QIB's pages, QIC's release or LinkedIn. A third-party snippet lists brokerage among its activities but was not verified.

digital_investing.detail: No app, portal or digital investing channel found. qinvest.com shows only a placeholder page stating a new website is coming (observed 2026-10-12).

advisory.detail: Institutional investment-banking advisory: LinkedIn lists advisory, M&A, ECM, DCM and sukuk as specialties; the Jul 2021 release says the co-CEOs would work on strategic transactions in the Middle East and Turkey. Not advisory to individual investors.

discretionary.detail: Asset Management division exists but whether it runs discretionary client mandates was not described in any opened source.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No model-portfolio or robo service found.

funds_platform.detail: No third-party fund shelf or platform found.

structured_products.detail: No structured products found; sukuk arranging for issuers is a capital-markets activity, not a client product.

private_markets.detail: Principal Investments division focused on real estate, credit and equity; LinkedIn lists private equity, real estate and funds among specialties. Specific current funds or deal sizes were not found.

islamic_wealth.detail: The whole firm is Shari'a-compliant ('Qatar's first Islamic Investment Bank' in the QIB Annual Report 2025); 49% of Epicure Islamic Investment Management; sukuk arranging.
